words: Okay, so the thing that stuck with me most was everything looking flat, like cut-out paper. Really bright colours, like reds and yellows and blues.
More like a place I could walk around in, but also sort of fake? Like the houses were leaning over the street, but everything was paper.
There were people everywhere, flat like cardboard cutouts, all going the same way. Then I saw my mum at a corner, folding something really carefully.
Yeah, I went up to her. She gave me what she was folding — a little red paper bird.
It felt light and a bit fragile, like if I held it too hard it would crease. I didn't want to mess it up.
I just kept it in my hand. Then it started to rain. But it wasn't water — it was hundreds of tiny paper birds, all different colours, landing on the street and on people's shoulders.
It was actually kind of calm, even though it was strange. They were just landing everywhere, not heavy. Then something else happened, though.
The whole city started folding up around us. The houses folded down flat one after another, like a pop-up book closing.
It wasn't scary exactly. More like it was just finishing, like everything was packing itself away. By the end it was just me and my mum standing on a big sheet of white paper. Then I woke up.
I don't remember what happened to the bird at that point. It might have still been in my hand, but I can't say for sure.
Probably the rain of paper birds. That's the bit I keep seeing in my head.
Yeah, it was weird but peaceful at the same time. I didn't want it to stop.
More just the way it looked. I don't remember any sound or smell, just all the birds coming down.
Yeah, that's basically it. You got it right.
